The '''71st Academy Awards''' ceremony, organized by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored the best of [[1998 in film]] and took place on March 21, 1999, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in Los Angeles beginning at 5:30&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 8:30&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 24 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Gil Cates]] and directed by Louis J. Horvitz.<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=231}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=233}}</ref> Actress [[Whoopi Goldberg]] hosted the show for the third time.<ref>{{cite news|title=Whoopi Goldberg to host Oscars |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/254295.stm |access-date=January 9, 2014 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=January 13, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109074732/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/254295.stm |archive-date=January 9, 2014}}</ref> She first hosted the [[66th Academy Awards|66th ceremony]] held in 1994 and had last hosted the [[68th Academy Awards|68th ceremony]] in 1996.<ref>{{cite news|last=Wallace |first=Amy |title=Whoopi Goldberg Gets Tapped to Host 71st Oscar Ceremony |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-jan-13-ca-62925-story.html |access-date=January 3, 2014 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=January 13, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131221141626/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/jan/13/entertainment/ca-62925 |archive-date=December 21, 2013}}</ref> Nearly a month earlier in a ceremony held at the [[Beverly Wilshire Hotel|Regent Beverly Wilshire Hotel]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]] on February 27, the [[Academy Award for Technical Achievement|Academy Awards for Technical Achievement]] were presented by host [[Anne Heche]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Graser |first=Marc |title=Avid has fan in Oscar at Sci-tech ceremony |url=https://variety.com/1999/digital/news/avid-has-fan-in-oscar-at-sci-tech-ceremony-1117491753/ |access-date=January 3, 2014 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=February 28, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104010431/http://variety.com/1999/digital/news/avid-has-fan-in-oscar-at-sci-tech-ceremony-1117491753/ |archive-date=January 4, 2014}}</ref>

''[[Shakespeare in Love]]'' won seven awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Rosen |first=Steven |title='Love', not war: Best-picture Oscar goes to 'Shakespeare' |work=[[The Denver Post]] |date=March 22, 1999 |page=A1}}</ref> Other winners included ''[[Saving Private Ryan]]'' with five awards, ''[[Life Is Beautiful]]'' with three, and ''[[Affliction (1997 film)|Affliction]]'', ''[[Bunny (1998 film)|Bunny]]'', ''[[Election Night (1998 film)|Election Night]]'', ''[[Elizabeth (film)|Elizabeth]]'', ''[[Gods and Monsters (film)|Gods and Monsters]]'', ''[[The Last Days]]'', ''[[The Personals: Improvisations on Romance in the Golden Years]]'', ''[[The Prince of Egypt]]'', and ''[[What Dreams May Come (film)|What Dreams May Come]]'' with one. The telecast garnered nearly 46 million viewers in the United States.

==Winners and nominees==
<!-- Please do not add any fact or statement below unless you have a credible source verifying it. Otherwise, it will be promptly removed. -->

The nominees for the 71st Academy Awards were announced on February 9, 1999, at the [[Samuel Goldwyn Theater]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]], by [[Robert Rehme]], president of the Academy, and the actor [[Kevin Spacey]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Munoz |first=Lorena |title=It's the Early Birds That Get to Squirm |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-feb-10-ca-6553-story.html |access-date=January 3, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=February 10, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104100303/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/feb/10/entertainment/ca-6553 |archive-date=January 4, 2014}}</ref> ''[[Shakespeare in Love]]'' earned the most nominations with 13; ''[[Saving Private Ryan]]'' came in second place with 11.<ref>{{cite news |last=Anthony |first=Todd |title=71st Academy Awards |url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1999-02-10/lifestyle/9902090688_1_71st-academy-awards-spielberg-private-ryan |access-date=January 3, 2014 |work=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |date=February 10, 1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202124337/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1999-02-10/lifestyle/9902090688_1_71st-academy-awards-spielberg-private-ryan |archive-date=February 2, 2014 }}</ref>

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 21, 1999.<ref>{{cite news|title=Oscar loves 'Shakespeare' Bard's film takes 7 Academy Awards; Benigni, Paltrow named best actors|work=[[San Antonio Express-News]]|date=March 22, 1999|page=1D}}</ref> ''[[Life Is Beautiful]]'' was the second film nominated simultaneously for Best Picture and Best Foreign Language Film in the same year (the first being ''[[Z (1969 film)|Z]]'' in [[42nd Academy Awards|1969]]).<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=401}}</ref> Best Actor winner [[Roberto Benigni]] was the second person to direct himself to an acting Oscar win. [[Laurence Olivier]] first achieved this feat for his performance in 1948's ''[[Hamlet (1948 film)|Hamlet]]''.<ref>{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=423}}</ref> He also became the fourth individual to earn acting, directing, screenwriting nominations for the same film.<ref>{{cite news|last=Welkos |first=Robert W. |title=Benigni Rising Has Hollywood Gushing |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-mar-19-ca-18710-story.html |access-date=January 7, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 19, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140108041903/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/19/entertainment/ca-18710 |archive-date=January 8, 2014}}</ref> In addition, Benigni was the third performer to [[List of actors nominated for Academy Awards for foreign language performances|win an Oscar for a non-English speaking role]].<ref>{{cite news|last=O'Neil |first=Tom |title=Quiz: Who won Oscars for foreign-lingo roles? |url=http://goldderby.latimes.com/awards_goldderby/2010/09/oscars-academy-awards-825916374-entertainment-news.html |access-date=January 13, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=September 22, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116134359/http://goldderby.latimes.com/awards_goldderby/2010/09/oscars-academy-awards-825916374-entertainment-news.html |archive-date=January 16, 2014}}</ref> Best Actress nominee [[Fernanda Montenegro]] was the first Latina to be nominated in that category.<ref>{{cite web|title=Latinos In The Oscars: Almost 60 Winners And Nominees Along The History Of The Academy Awards! [Photos]|url=http://www.latintimes.com/latinos-oscars-almost-60-winners-and-nominees-along-history-academy-awards-photos-297193#slide/6|access-date=October 27, 2014|language=en|archive-date=February 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150224085004/http://www.latintimes.com/latinos-oscars-almost-60-winners-and-nominees-along-history-academy-awards-photos-297193#slide/6|url-status=dead}}</ref>
By virtue of their nominations for portraying Queen [[Elizabeth I of England]], Best Actress nominee [[Cate Blanchett]] and Best Supporting Actress winner [[Judi Dench]] became the first pair of actresses to earn acting nominations in the same year for portraying the same character in different films.<ref>{{harvnb|Kinn|Piazza|2002|p=299}}</ref>

==Ceremony information==
[[File:Whoopi Goldberg at a NYC No on Proposition 8 Rally.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|[[Whoopi Goldberg]] hosted the 71st Academy Awards]]

Riding on the success of the [[70th Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]] which garnered record-high viewership figures and several [[Emmy Awards|Emmy]]s, AMPAS sought changes to the festivities that would help build upon this recent success. In June 1998, Academy president [[Robert Rehme]] announced that the show would be held on a Sunday for the first time in history.<ref name="Sunday">{{cite news|last=Madigan |first=Nick |title=Sunday officially Oscar's |url=https://variety.com/1998/film/news/sunday-officially-oscar-s-1117477950/ |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=Variety |date=June 26, 1998 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110222613/http://variety.com/1998/film/news/sunday-officially-oscar-s-1117477950/ |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> AMPAS and network [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] hoped to capitalize on the high television ratings and viewership that benefit programs airing on that particular day of the week.<ref>{{cite news|last=Welkos |first=Robert W. |title=Cinema's Super Sunday |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-mar-13-ca-16738-story.html |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 13, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110224511/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/13/entertainment/ca-16738 |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> The Academy also stated that the move to Sunday would ease concerns about traffic gridlock and transportation that are significantly lower on weekends.<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=213}}</ref> Additionally, AMPAS decided to continue producing the ceremony and presenting a finished feed to ABC, instead of entrusting production to the network, similarly as [[70th Academy Awards|last year]].<ref name="Sunday"/>

The following January, [[Gil Cates]] was selected as a producer of the telecast.<ref>{{cite news|last=Madigan |first=Nick |title=Cates to produce Oscars |url=https://variety.com/1999/film/news/cates-to-produce-oscars-1117489884/ |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=Variety |date=January 4, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110233415/http://variety.com/1999/film/news/cates-to-produce-oscars-1117489884/ |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> He immediately selected Oscar-winning actress [[Whoopi Goldberg]] as host of the 1999 ceremony.<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=214}}</ref> Cates explained his decision to bring back Goldberg as host saying, "The audience adores Whoopi and that affection, plus Whoopi's extraordinary talent makes her a terrific host for the show."<ref name="CNN">{{cite news|title=Whoopi! Goldberg to host Oscars |url=http://www.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/News/9901/13/showbuzz/#story1 |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=[[CNN]] |date=January 13, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304111907/http://www.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/News/9901/13/showbuzz/ |archive-date=March 4, 2016}}</ref> In a statement, Goldberg expressed that she was honored and excited to be selected to emcee the telecast commenting, "I am thrilled to escort Oscar into the new millennium. Who would have thought that I would be hosting the last Oscar telecast of the century? It's a huge deal."<ref name="CNN"/>

{{multiple image

Several other people participated in the production of the ceremony and its related events. [[Bill Conti]] served as musical director for the festivities.<ref>{{cite news|title=Morning Report: Arts And Entertainment Reports From The Times, News Services And The Nations's Press |url=https://articles.latimes.com/1999/jan/23/entertainment/ca-739/2 |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=January 23, 1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110093511/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/jan/23/entertainment/ca-739/2 |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> In addition to supervising the Best Song nominee performances, choreographer [[Debbie Allen]] produced a dance number featuring five dancers from around the world showcasing the nominees for Best Original Dramatic Score.<ref>{{harvnb|Pond|2005|p=199}}</ref> For the first time, the Academy produced its own [[Academy Awards pre-show|pre-show]] that preceded the main telecast. Produced by Dennis Doty, the half-hour program was hosted by actress [[Geena Davis]] and [[CNN]] reporter [[Jim Moret]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Shister |first=Gail |title=CNN's Jim Moret Working Swing Shift On Oscar Night |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1999/03/18/cnns-jim-moret-working-swing-shift-on-oscar-night/ |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=Chicago Tribune |date=March 18, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110224619/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1999-03-18/features/9903180292_1_jim-moret-showbiz-today-oscar-preview-show |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> Similar to coverage of red carpet arrivals on networks such as [[E!]], the pre-show featured interviews with nominees and other guests, recaps of nominations and segments highlighting behind-the-scenes preparations for the telecast.<ref>{{harvnb|Pond|2005|p=211}}</ref>

===Box office performance of nominees===
At the time of the nominations announcement on February 9, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees was $302&nbsp;million with an average of $60.4&nbsp;million per film.<ref name=BoxOfficeMojoOscars>{{cite news|title=1998 Academy Award Nominations and Winner for Best Picture |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1998&p=.htm |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=[[Box Office Mojo]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110155249/http://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1998&p=.htm |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> ''Saving Private Ryan'' was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees with $194.2&nbsp;million in domestic box office receipts. The film was followed by ''Shakespeare in Love'' ($36.5&nbsp;million), ''The Thin Red Line'' ($30.6&nbsp;million), ''Elizabeth'' ($21.5&nbsp;million), and finally ''Life is Beautiful'' ($18.4&nbsp;million).<ref name=BoxOfficeMojoOscars />

Of the top 50 grossing movies of the year, 36 nominations went to 13 films on the list. Only ''Saving Private Ryan'' (2nd), ''The Truman Show'' (11th), ''A Civil Action'' (40th) and ''Primary Colors'' (50th) were nominated for Best Picture, directing, acting or screenwriting.<ref name="boxofficemojooscars">{{cite web|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1999-02-08&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1998&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |title=1998 Domestic Grosses |work=Box Office Mojo |access-date=January 10, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110155234/http://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1999-02-08&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1998&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were ''Armageddon'' (1st), ''A Bug's Life'' (5th), ''Patch Adams'' (12th), ''Mulan'' (13th), ''The Mask of Zorro'' (17th), ''The Prince of Egypt'' (18th), ''The Horse Whisperer'' (24th), ''What Dreams May Come'' (37th) and ''Pleasantville'' (49th).<ref name="boxofficemojooscars" />

===Critical reviews===
The show received a mixed reception from media publications. Columnist [[Lisa Schwarzbaum]] of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' quipped that "Whoopi bombed last night, she knew it—and yet, crassly, she took it as a sign of her own outrageousness."<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Schawrzbaum |first=Lisa |title=Vulgar disfavors |url=https://ew.com/article/1999/03/22/lisa-schwarzbaum-critiques-oscars/ |access-date=January 9, 2014 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=March 22, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109225714/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0%2C%2C82753%2C00.html |archive-date=January 9, 2014}}</ref> ''[[The Washington Post]]'' television critic [[Tom Shales]] bemoaned that Goldberg "spent a great deal of time laughing at her own jokes, many of which were dirty, a few dirty." He also lambasted the host's presentation of the five Best Costume Design nominees calling it time-consuming and tasteless.<ref name="Oscar review">{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=244}}</ref> Film critic John Hartl of ''[[The Seattle Times]]'' lamented that the telecast "was the longest and possibly the dullest Oscar show of the century, clocking in at four hours."<ref>{{cite news|last=Hartl |first=John |title='Love' Conquers All{{ndash}}Oscar Gets Fickle In Night Of Close Calls And Upsets |url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19990322/2950840/love-conquers-all----oscar-gets-fickle-in-night-of-close-calls-and-upsets |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |date=March 22, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110090846/http://community.seattletimes.nwsource.com/archive/?date=19990322&slug=2950840 |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref>

Other media outlets received the broadcast more positively. Television columnist Robert Bianco of ''[[USA Today]]'' commended Goldberg's hosting performance writing that he liked "the sharper, more socially conscious edge Goldberg brings."<ref>{{cite news|last=Bianco|first=Robert|title=Show makes lead of Hollywood gold|work=[[USA Today]]|date=March 22, 1999|page=D1}}</ref> ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' television critic Matthew Gilbert commented, "It was the perfect year with more than enough Hollywood intrigue and a battle for her to play off."<ref name="Oscar review" /> Joanne Ostrow of ''[[The Denver Post]]'' raved that "Whoopi definitely was on, more so than in her two previous hosting stints." She added that "the show was exceptionally smooth."<ref>{{cite news|last=Ostrow |first=Joanne |title=The African Queen trumps Billy Crystal |work=The Denver Post |date=March 22, 1999 |url=http://extras.denverpost.com/scene/oscar0322c.htm |access-date=January 10, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110205302/http://extras.denverpost.com/scene/oscar0322c.htm |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on ABC drew an average of 45.51 million viewers over its length, which was an 18% decrease from the previous year's ceremony.<ref name="LA Times Oscar Ratings">{{cite news|last=Lowry |first=Brian |title=Oscars Draw Big Numbers, Though Not as Big as Hoped |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-mar-23-ca-20046-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=January 10, 2014 |date=March 23, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110093449/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/23/entertainment/ca-20046 |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> An estimated 78.10 million total viewers watched all or part of the awards.<ref name="LA Times Oscar Ratings" /> The show also drew lower [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony with 28.63% of households watching over a 47.79 share.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bierbaum |first=Tom |title=Oscars don't push aud envelope |url=https://variety.com/1999/tv/news/oscars-don-t-push-aud-envelope-1117492582/ |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=Variety |date=March 22, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110233148/http://variety.com/1999/tv/news/oscars-don-t-push-aud-envelope-1117492582/ |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref> It also drew a lower 18{{ndash}}49 demo rating with an 18.85 rating over a 37.31 share among viewers in that demographic.<ref name="TVB Oscars">{{cite news|title=Academy Awards ratings |work=[[Television Bureau of Advertising]] |url=http://www.tvb.org/media/file/Academy_Awards.pdf |access-date=June 27, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130515152338/http://www.tvb.org/media/file/Academy_Awards.pdf |archive-date=May 15, 2013}}</ref>

In July 1999, the show received seven nominations at the [[51st Primetime Emmy Awards]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Primetime Emmy database |url=http://www.emmys.com/shows/71st-annual-academy-awards |access-date=January 9, 2014 |work=Academy of Television Arts and Sciences |publisher=ATAS |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140109223435/http://www.emmys.com/shows/71st-annual-academy-awards |archive-date=January 9, 2014}}</ref> Two months later, the ceremony won two of those nominations for Outstanding Art Direction for a Variety or Music Program ([[Roy Christopher]] and Stephen Olson) and Outstanding Lighting Direction for a Drama Series, Variety Series, Miniseries, Movie, or Special (Robert Dickinson, Robert T. Barnhart, Andy O'Reilly, Matt Ford).<ref>{{cite news|title=51st Annual Emmy Awards: Creative Arts Emmy Winners |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-sep-13-ca-9838-story.html |access-date=January 10, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=September 13, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110091506/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/sep/13/entertainment/ca-9838 |archive-date=January 10, 2014}}</ref>

=="In Memoriam"==
The annual "In Memoriam" tribute was presented by actress [[Annette Bening]]. The montage featured an excerpt of the main title from ''[[Ever After]]'' composed by [[George Fenton]].<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=237}}</ref>

A separate tribute to actor, singer and former Oscar host [[Frank Sinatra]] was presented by [[John Travolta]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Carter |first=Bill |title=After the Oscars, The Complaints |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/03/24/movies/tv-notes-after-the-oscars-the-complaints.html |access-date=January 8, 2014 |work=The New York Times |date=March 24, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140121060023/http://www.nytimes.com/1999/03/24/movies/tv-notes-after-the-oscars-the-complaints.html |archive-date=January 21, 2014}}</ref> Later, actor Val Kilmer presented one to actors [[Gene Autry]] and [[Roy Rogers]].<ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=235}}</ref> After the ''In Memoriam'' segment was shown, host Goldberg and director [[Steven Spielberg]] eulogized film critic [[Gene Siskel]] and director [[Stanley Kubrick]] respectively.<ref name=Tribute>{{cite news|last=Warren |first=Ellen |title=Oscar Night Salute To Siskel Was All Whoopi |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1999/03/23/oscar-night-salute-to-siskel-was-all-whoopi/ |access-date=January 8, 2014 |work=Chicago Tribune |date=March 23, 1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140108050235/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1999-03-23/news/9903230096_1_siskel-oscar-val-kilmer |archive-date=January 8, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Bona|2002|p=238}}</ref>
